scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Kaşık Havası, known in Turkish as Kaşık Oyunları and in Greek as Khoros koutalion, developed as a widespread folk tradition across the Mediterranean region.

Classified as both a Turkish and Greek folk dance form, the tradition evolved alongside regional folk singing and vernacular music traditions, historically incorporating archaic instruments such as the beast bow before the adoption of the modern violin.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Performances are accompanied by folk songs set typically in 2/4 or 4/4 time.

The instrumental ensemble historically featured the beast bow, which was later superseded by the violin, accompanied by the bağlama (long-necked lute) and clarinet, with the percussive clicking of wooden spoons played directly by the dancers.
Listen for the wooden spoons, beast bow, violin, bağlama.
The pulse is 2/4 or 4/4.

Kaşık Havası is immediately recognized by the sharp, crisp clatter of wooden spoons played in steady 2/4 or 4/4 meter. The bright percussion interlocks with acoustic melodies led by clarinet and bağlama, underpinned historically by the beast bow or violin and accompanied by vernacular folk singing.

narration: The dance exists across Turkish and Greek folk settings under the names Kaşık Havası, Kaşık Oyunları, and Khoros koutalion, displaying a varying structure in arrangement, performance, rhythm, and melodic contours across the Mediterranean region.
